finding_dispositions.note: USCCB 2026 calendar, 2002 Missal, Normae universales, General Calendar, 2008 variation list, ICEL Antiphonary, OLM 1981 and the dated USCCB readings page were fetched whole over verified TLS, matched to their registered or recorded SHA-256, re-read at the cited loci and bound; new passage records for Week XXV (pp. 288-289), OLM no. 133, Praenotanda 105-107, Tabella II, the 20 September calendar entry, the Antiphonary page and GIRM 48, 51, 53, 61-64, 68, 74, 87, 364. The GIRM chapter responses differ by two bytes from the registered states, so they are registered as new dated artifacts and the existing 363/365 passage records are bound as catalogued only. A recomputed seal lists files under every owner.

Both --check runs traced under a Python audit hook: 1,590 repository files opened, 1,576 beneath src/, 153 of which (80 Revised Version, 73 WEB Catholic verse files) lay outside the first seal. Both edition directories are declared; the recomputed seal contains every src/ file the runs open.

Option (a): Migne PL 24, Paris 1865 (Vallarsi's text), Internet Archive item sanctieusebiihie04jero, fetched whole over verified TLS, registered with its complete OCR and a four-page facsimile (both title pages, cols. 553-556) retained. All six quotations verified on page images with columns. The earlier remote delivery is no longer bound. Certificate verification was never disabled.

Added, each read at an exact locus: Jerome on Matthew 20 (PL 26, page images), Aquinas on Matthew 20 and John 10:14 (Venice 1745; the quoted sentences on page images, the rest of the Matthew lecture in OCR only), Aquinas on Philippians 1 (Dessain 1857 facsimile), Hilary on Psalm 118:4-5 and Psalm 144 (CSEL 22 page images), Bellarmine on both psalms (abridged 1866 English), Bede on Acts 16:14-15 (PL 92 page image) with a bounded negative for later comment on 14b, and Augustine Tract. 47.3-5. Limits that remain are stated in scope sections 4, 5 and 10.

Scope section 7 now confines the Augustine-Chrysostom difference to Acts 16:14, states that Sermo 87.8 concerns the labourers' ignorance of the wage and that Sermo 87 does not address lateness; interpretations Reading 3 and the Comparison were made consistent.
